nora-peopleops: Quick Q  Vivek's spouse is on H-4 and applied for H-4 EAD. Card is delayed; offer start 09/01. Can we onboard him if spouse's EAD arrives late? @sara-legal

vivek-candidate: Hi team  spouse filed I-765 on 06/10, got biometrics, USCIS status says 'Case Was Received'. We expected card mid-August. I will be physically in the US at start date on H-1 with H-1 approval already. Concern is dependent spouse work auth and benefits for family coverage.

sara-legal: Since Vivek himself is H-1 and has valid I-797 and stamping, his own employment/I-9 is fine. The spouse's EAD only matters if spouse will be employed by Redwood. For benefits (health), we can enroll dependents without EAD. Payroll/T&C: if spouse will work for us, they need their own work authorization docs to be on payroll.

alex-payroll: Confirming  dependents can be added to benefits with passport and birth/marriage certs. Payroll needs SSN for dependents only if claiming on flexible spending accounts; otherwise it's optional. If spouse starts work at Redwood, we need EAD scanned for I-9.

nora-peopleops: OK. So action items: 1) Proceed with Vivek hire as planned; 2) Allow spouse enrollment in benefits once marriage docs uploaded; 3) If spouse later wants to join as employee, require EAD before payroll.

it-bot: Reminder: upload docs here: https://onboard.redwood.ai/upload (choose 'benefits' or 'work auth').

vivek-candidate: Got it. Spouse will not be starting at Redwood immediately. Will upload marriage cert and passport. Thanks.

sara-legal: Also flag: if spouse travels internationally before EAD arrives and later returns on H-4, re-entry timelines can affect EAD processing in some cases. We'll send a short advisory note.

 nora-peopleops: I'll update offer packet and benefits checklist and close unless other questions. Marking in-progress.
